entries.statement: In ShardedQueue::push, `self.max_shard_pushed.fetch_max(index, Release)` uses Release ordering where AcqRel is required. Release on a read-modify-write does not order the subsequent shard push against the index update, so `self.shards[index].push(task)` may be sequenced before the fetch_max and a consumer reading max_shard_pushed can miss the task.
entries.source_ref: ADD-SP, PR #7757 review thread, 2025-12-08: 'With the Release ordering, compiler might reorder the self.shards[index].push(task) and fetch_max, which means that the .push(task) might be sequenced-before the fetch_max.'
entries.admission_evidence: Present at checkpoint. Verified in the fixture: `git grep 'fetch_max(index, Release)'` matches sharded_queue.rs at this head. NOT present at merge — `max_shard_pushed` and `fetch_max` were removed entirely during review (final head 9de7950e59f8 contains no fetch_max).
entries.must_flag: Flags that the fetch_max on the shard-index counter uses Release where AcqRel is needed, permitting the shard push to be reordered relative to the index update. Equivalent framings count (a memory-ordering bug on this RMW, a missing acquire side, a visibility gap between push and index).

entries.statement: The queue acquires a shard lock while already holding the condvar lock — nested locking, which is error-prone and a deadlock hazard.
entries.source_ref: ADD-SP, PR #7757 review thread, 2025-12-11: 'Here, we attempt to acquire the shard lock while holding the condvar lock, this is the nested locking pattern...'
entries.admission_evidence: PROVISIONAL — the nested-lock structure is present at the checkpoint, but the thread was written against a later head (2025-12-11) and the exact lock pairing must be re-verified against this checkpoint before this entry is scored.
entries.must_flag: Flags that a shard lock is taken while the condvar lock is held.

There is no defect statement to write a must_flag against, so this cannot be scored. A reviewer cannot be graded on finding a defect nobody has diagnosed.
